title: Are schools a great equalizer? They help kids catch up, but wealthier children still pull ahead

paragraphs.english: This page is an independently written reading guide to an article published by The Conversation on 4 November 2026. The author is David Blazar, a scholar of education policy at the University of Maryland, writing about research he carried out with colleagues. The original article is linked at the foot of the page. What follows is a guide to the argument and to the way the numbers are built, written for readers who want to take the English slowly. It is not a translation of the piece.
paragraphs.chinese: 本页是为《The Conversation》2026 年 11 月 4 日发表的一篇文章独立撰写的阅读导读。作者 David Blazar 是马里兰大学研究教育政策的学者，文章介绍的是他与同事合作完成的研究。原文链接见本页页尾。以下是就这篇文章的论证、以及它如何搭建数字所写的导读，面向希望慢慢读英文的读者；它不是原文的翻译。

paragraphs.english: The article begins with a quotation and a date. In 1848 the education reformer Horace Mann described public schooling as the great equalizer of the conditions of men. More than 175 years later, the author notes, scholars are still arguing about whether he was right — and the answer, in this piece, is a carefully qualified yes.
paragraphs.chinese: 文章以一则引语和一个年份开头。1848 年，教育改革者 Horace Mann 把公立学校教育称作“人类境况的伟大平衡器”。作者指出，175 多年过去，学者们仍在争论他说得对不对——而在这篇文章里，答案是经过谨慎限定的“对”。

paragraphs.english: Two bodies of evidence pull in opposite directions, and the opening paragraphs set them side by side. One line of research finds that a child's family background shapes academic achievement far more than school does. Another finds that schools narrow gaps that would otherwise be even wider. Both can be true at once, which is the tension the rest of the article works through.
paragraphs.chinese: 两组证据指向相反方向，开头几段把它们并排摆出。一类研究发现，孩子的家庭背景对其学业成就的塑造远大于学校。另一类则发现，学校缩小了本来会更大的差距。两者可以同时成立，而这正是文章余下部分要处理的张力。

paragraphs.english: The classic illustration is a study that followed children in Baltimore in the 1980s. Low-income and wealthier children learned at roughly similar rates during the school year; the gap widened over the summer, when some children read with their parents, visited libraries and went to camp while others did not. The author is careful with this evidence, noting that how much summer learning loss really exists is still an open question. The larger point survives the caveat, though: the differences are already large on the first day of kindergarten, and for a given group of students they then stay about the same size through the school years.
paragraphs.chinese: 经典例证是一项追踪 1980 年代巴尔的摩儿童的研究。低收入与较富裕的孩子在学年中学习速度大致相近；差距在暑假拉开——有的孩子和父母一起读书、去图书馆、参加夏令营，有的没有。作者对这组证据很谨慎，指出暑期学习损失究竟有多大仍是一个未决问题。但更大的论点经得起这一保留：差距在幼儿园第一天就已经很大，而对同一批学生来说，此后在整个求学阶段大致保持不变。

paragraphs.english: What the new research does is change the question. Instead of asking how much students learn at school, the team asked what students receive, in school and out of it: funding, support services, and the time that schools, government programmes and families put into each child.
paragraphs.chinese: 这项新研究做的是换一个问题。研究者不问学生在校学到了多少，而问学生得到了什么——校内外皆是如此：经费、支持性服务，以及学校、政府项目与家庭在每个孩子身上投入的时间。

paragraphs.english: The method is worth following, because the conclusion depends on it. The researchers combined ten nationally representative government surveys and tracked 77 kinds of investment, from teachers and tutoring to housing, food and childcare, plus factors with no direct price tag such as the time parents spend reading with a child. They then put a dollar value on each item — valuing a parent's time at the average hourly wage, for instance — so that everything could be added up and compared across families.
paragraphs.chinese: 方法值得跟一遍，因为结论依赖于它。研究者合并了十项具有全国代表性的政府调查，追踪 77 类“投入”，从教师、辅导到住房、食物与托育，还包括没有直接价格标签的因素，比如父母陪孩子读书的时间。随后他们给每一项折算美元——例如按平均小时工资给父母的时间定价——这样一切都能加总，并在不同家庭之间比较。

paragraphs.english: The total is striking in its ordinariness. Counting government spending, family spending and parental time together, the average child in the United States receives about $502,000 between birth and the age of 18.
paragraphs.chinese: 总数以其平淡无奇而引人注意。把政府支出、家庭支出与父母时间合在一起计算，美国孩子从出生到 18 岁平均获得约 50.2 万美元。

paragraphs.english: The gaps start early. Before the age of five, children in the poorest quarter of families receive roughly $44,000 less in total investment than children in the richest quarter, a difference of 24 per cent, and most of that early shortfall comes from housing and childcare costs.
paragraphs.chinese: 差距很早就开始。五岁之前，最贫穷四分之一家庭的孩子所得总投入比最富裕四分之一家庭的孩子少约 4.4 万美元，差距为 24%；这一早期缺口主要来自住房与托育成本。

paragraphs.english: Then comes the finding that gives the article its shape. As children move into elementary school, the investment gap between the richest and poorest quarters is cut in half, from 24 per cent to 12 per cent. For Black children the effect is larger still: the gap between Black and white children shrinks from 20 per cent in the early years to 7 per cent once kindergarten begins.
paragraphs.chinese: 接着是赋予文章骨架的发现。当孩子进入小学，最富与最穷四分之一之间的投入差距缩小一半，从 24% 降到 12%。对黑人儿童而言，效果更大：黑人与白人儿童之间的差距从幼儿期的 20% 缩小到幼儿园开始后的 7%。

paragraphs.english: That matters because spending is not decorative. Research cited in the piece shows that more school spending improves achievement and long-term outcomes, especially for students from low-income families. Public education, on this account, really does act as an equalizer — for the years in which children are inside it.
paragraphs.chinese: 这一点重要，是因为支出并非装饰。文中引用的研究表明，更多学校支出能改善学业成就与长期结果，对低收入家庭的学生尤其如此。按此说法，公共教育确实起到了平衡器的作用——在孩子身处其中的那些年里。

paragraphs.english: So the puzzle sharpens: if investment evens out at school, why do achievement gaps not close? The author's answer is that money buys different things for different children. Once children are in school, those from the lowest-income families receive 72 per cent more in tutoring and 68 per cent more in special education than those from the highest-income families, and Black children receive more than twice as much tutoring as white children. These services are designed to help students catch up. The article's neat formulation is that a dollar spent catching up is not the same as a dollar spent getting ahead.
paragraphs.chinese: 于是谜题更清楚了：如果入学后投入趋于持平，为什么学业差距没有闭合？作者的答案是，钱对不同孩子买到了不同的东西。孩子入学后，最低收入家庭的孩子获得的辅导比最高收入家庭的孩子多 72%，特殊教育多 68%；黑人孩子获得的辅导是白人孩子的两倍多。这些服务意在帮学生“追上来”。文章有一句简洁的说法：花在追赶上的美元，和花在领先上的美元不是一回事。

paragraphs.english: Tutoring is the clearest case. It has long been one of schools' main catch-up tools, and since the pandemic schools have leaned on it more heavily than ever. The evidence for it is genuinely strong: studies that assign students to tutoring at random find some of the largest test-score gains of any school programme. Federal money made a bigger push possible — Congress sent schools nearly $190 billion, with the largest round distributed on the same formula as the long-standing Title I funding for high-poverty districts — and by 2022-23 more than a third of public schools offered high-dosage tutoring, meaning frequent sessions in small groups.
paragraphs.chinese: 辅导是最清楚的例子。它长期是学校主要的补差工具，疫情以来学校对它的倚重超过以往。相关证据确实有力：随机分配学生接受辅导的研究发现，其测验分数提升幅度是各类学校项目中最大的之一。联邦资金让更大规模的推进成为可能——国会向学校拨了近 1900 亿美元，其中最大一轮按长期用于高贫困学区的 Title I 公式分配——到 2022-23 学年，超过三分之一的公立学校提供“高剂量”辅导，即频繁的小组课程。

paragraphs.english: But for many low-income, Black and Latino students, tutoring was not new. In the study's data, collected between 2014 and 2021, about 17 per cent of school-age children were being tutored, including 25 per cent of Black children and 19 per cent of Latino children, against 14 per cent of white children. Among Black, Latino and low-income children who received tutoring, more than three-quarters got that support from public schools.
paragraphs.chinese: 但对许多低收入、黑人与拉丁裔学生来说，辅导并不新鲜。在研究采集的 2014 至 2021 年数据中，约 17% 的学龄儿童接受辅导，其中黑人儿童 25%、拉丁裔儿童 19%，白人儿童为 14%。在接受辅导的黑人、拉丁裔与低收入儿童中，超过四分之三的辅导由公立学校提供。

paragraphs.english: The results of all this effort are sobering. Early in the recovery the share of students being tutored did not appear to grow much; a nationally representative survey of parents in autumn 2022 put it at about 15 per cent. Meanwhile the pandemic widened achievement gaps, and students in high-poverty districts still trail those in wealthier districts by more than students in the same grades did before 2020. Federal relief money helped, but it did not restore the earlier position.
paragraphs.chinese: 这些努力的结果并不令人乐观。复苏初期，接受辅导的学生比例似乎没有增长多少；2022 年秋一项全国代表性家长调查显示约为 15%。与此同时，疫情拉大了学业差距，高贫困学区的学生如今落后富裕学区的幅度，仍大于 2020 年前同年级学生的差距。联邦救助资金起了作用，但没有恢复到先前的位置。

paragraphs.english: Catch-up help is only half the picture, and the second half is where the argument lands. Wealthier children also receive more of the resources that help them pull ahead. Low-income students and students of colour are more likely than richer, white students to have newer, less experienced teachers, a pattern the study documents as well as earlier work. Outside school the differences are starker still: wealthier families invest far more in music lessons, sport and other enrichment, and by 2024 the richest tenth of families spent more than 13 times as much per child as the poorest quarter on childcare, education and extracurricular activities — up from about three times as much in the early 1980s.
paragraphs.chinese: 补差只是图景的一半，另一半才是论证落点。较富裕的孩子还获得更多帮助他们领先的资源。低收入学生与有色人种学生比更富裕的白人学生更可能遇到新手、经验较少的教师，这一模式既有早先研究指出，本次研究也有记录。校外差异更明显：富裕家庭在音乐课、体育与其他拓展活动上投入远多，到 2024 年，最富裕十分之一家庭在每个孩子身上的托育、教育与课外活动支出，是最贫穷四分之一家庭的 13 倍以上——而 1980 年代初约为 3 倍。

paragraphs.english: The conclusion is therefore narrower than the headline question, and more useful. Public education is the main reason the investment gap between rich and poor children shrinks once children turn five. But equal spending is not equal opportunity: much of the extra school spending on low-income, Black and Latino children goes to making up for gaps that opened before they started school, while wealthier children keep collecting the experienced teachers and enrichment that help them move ahead. If schools are to close gaps rather than merely stop them widening, more catch-up help will not be enough on its own. And because the widest gaps open before kindergarten, in housing and childcare where public support is thinnest, the problem cannot be left to schools alone.
paragraphs.chinese: 因此结论比标题式提问更窄，也更有用。公共教育是孩子五岁后贫富投入差距缩小的主要原因。但支出均等不等于机会均等：用在低收入、黑人与拉丁裔孩子身上的额外学校支出，很大一部分用于弥补他们入学前就已形成的缺口，而富裕孩子则持续积累帮助他们前进的经验教师与拓展资源。若学校要真正闭合差距而非仅仅阻止其扩大，单靠更多补差帮助不够。而由于最大缺口在幼儿园之前、在公共支持最薄的住房与托育领域形成，这个问题不能只留给学校。

paragraphs.english: For a reader working on English, the piece is a lesson in how a quantitative argument is assembled. Notice how many of its claims are hedged: by some measures, about, roughly, more likely, still an open question. Each qualifier narrows the sentence it sits in, and each is the part a hurried reader drops. Notice also that the article keeps two different quantities apart — what is invested and what is achieved — and never lets one stand in for the other.
paragraphs.chinese: 对练英语的读者来说，这篇文章是一堂关于如何搭建定量论证的课。注意它有多少判断被加了限定：按某些衡量方式、大约、大致、更可能、仍是未决问题。每个限定词都收窄了它所在的那句话，而每个限定词都是匆忙的读者容易漏掉的部分。还要注意，文章始终把两种量分开——投入了什么、达成了什么——从不让其中一个代替另一个。

paragraphs.english: There is useful vocabulary in the way the author names his object. "Investment" and "enrichment" turn activities into countable things; "high-dosage" borrows a phrase from medicine to describe frequent small-group teaching; "catch-up" against "get ahead" sets two directions of spending against each other in three words. Comparison structures carry much of the meaning too, as in "more than 13 times as much per child as the poorest quarter" and "up from about three times as much in the early 1980s", where the second half quietly supplies the history that makes the first half alarming.
paragraphs.chinese: 作者给研究对象命名的方式里也有可用的词汇。investment 与 enrichment 把活动变成可计数之物；high-dosage 借用医学说法描述频繁的小组教学；catch-up 对 get ahead，用三个词把两种方向的支出对置起来。比较结构也承担了大量意义，例如“more than 13 times as much per child as the poorest quarter”与“up from about three times as much in the early 1980s”，后半句悄悄提供了让前半句显得惊人的历史。

paragraphs.english: Here is an editor-written practice sentence, not a quotation from the original article: Even if every district spent exactly the same amount on each child, the families able to pay for music lessons, tutors and summer camps would still send their children to the classroom door with advantages that no catch-up programme, however well funded, can fully undo.
paragraphs.chinese: 下面是一句由本站编辑自拟的练习句，并非原文引用：即便每个学区在每个孩子身上的支出完全相同，那些付得起音乐课、家教与夏令营的家庭，仍会把孩子送进教室门口，并带着任何补差项目——无论资金多么充足——都无法完全抵消的优势。

paragraphs.english: It is worth being explicit about what the article does not claim. It does not say that schools make no difference, nor that money is wasted on poor students; it says that the same dollar does different work depending on which side of the gap a child starts from. Nor is it a study of achievement itself — it measures investment, and then connects that measure to other research on outcomes. That distinction is the one to keep hold of, both as a reader and as someone likely to meet versions of this argument in other places.
paragraphs.chinese: 值得明确说出文章没有主张什么。它没说学校毫无作用，也没说花在贫困学生身上的钱被浪费；它说的是，同一美元起的作用不同，取决于孩子从差距的哪一侧起步。它也不是对学业成就本身的研究——它衡量的是投入，再把这一衡量与其他关于结果的研究连接起来。这个区别值得记住，无论作为读者，还是作为一个很可能在别处再遇到这套论证的人。

paragraphs.english: The final paragraph pushes the conclusion past the school gate. If the widest gaps open before children arrive, then the institutions that shape those first years — housing, childcare, the support available to parents — are part of the same argument, and pretending otherwise leaves schools doing repair work with tools designed for something else. That is a policy claim, and a reader is free to disagree with it. But the numbers behind it are laid out clearly enough to argue with, which is more than can be said for most claims about equality.
paragraphs.chinese: 最后一段把结论推过校门。如果最大缺口在孩子到校之前就已形成，那么塑造最初这些年的制度——住房、托育、给父母的支持——就是同一论证的一部分；假装不是，只会让学校用为别的目的设计的工具做修补工作。这是一个政策主张，读者完全可以不同意。但它背后的数字摆得足够清楚，足以让人与之争辩，而这已经比大多数关于平等的说法强得多。

sentenceNotes.sentence: Once children are in school, those from the lowest-income families receive 72 per cent more in tutoring and 68 per cent more in special education than those from the highest-income families, and Black children receive more than twice as much tutoring as white children.
sentenceNotes.mainClause: those from the lowest-income families receive 72 per cent more in tutoring and 68 per cent more in special education
sentenceNotes.structure: Once 引导时间状语从句；主句用两个 more ... than 比较结构并列（72 per cent more in tutoring / 68 per cent more in special education）；and 引出第三个比较分句，用 twice as much ... as 结构，省略了重复的 receive。
sentenceNotes.translation: 孩子一旦入学，来自最低收入家庭的所得辅导比最高收入家庭的孩子多 72%，特殊教育服务多 68%；黑人孩子获得的辅导是白人孩子的两倍多。
sentenceNotes.tip: 三个比较结构连着出现时，先找出每个 than / as ... as 后面的比较对象，再回头读数字；more 后面跟的是不可数的服务量，所以用 much 而不是 many。

sentenceNotes.sentence: If schools are to close gaps rather than merely stop them widening, more catch-up help will not be enough on its own.
sentenceNotes.mainClause: more catch-up help will not be enough on its own
sentenceNotes.structure: If 引导条件状语从句，从句中 be to 表示要达到某种目的；rather than 连接两个不定式（close / stop），形成对照；主句是主系表结构，on its own 作状语限定单靠本身。
sentenceNotes.translation: 如果学校要真正缩小差距，而不只是阻止差距继续扩大，那么仅靠更多补差性质的帮助是不够的。
sentenceNotes.tip: be to do 在条件句里常表示目的或设想；rather than 前后要接同形式的成分，这里是 close 与 stop 两个动词原形，读的时候可以把它换成而不是来验证结构是否对称。

sentenceNotes.sentence: Even if every district spent exactly the same amount on each child, the families able to pay for music lessons, tutors and summer camps would still send their children to the classroom door with advantages that no catch-up programme, however well funded, can fully undo.
sentenceNotes.mainClause: the families would still send their children to the classroom door with advantages
sentenceNotes.structure: 本句为编辑自拟的练习句。Even if 引导让步状语从句，用虚拟语气 spent / would send 表示假设；able to pay for ... 是后置形容词短语修饰 families；that no catch-up programme ... can fully undo 是定语从句修饰 advantages，从句中 however well funded 是插入的让步成分。
sentenceNotes.translation: 即便每个学区在每个孩子身上的支出完全相同，那些付得起音乐课、家教与夏令营的家庭，仍会把孩子送进教室门口，并带着任何补差项目——无论资金多么充足——都无法完全抵消的优势。
sentenceNotes.tip: 这是 editor-written practice sentence，不是原文引用。读长句时先剥掉插入语（however well funded），再看定语从句修饰的是哪个名词：这里 that 从句修饰 advantages，而不是 door。
